defectsFound.observed: Bite 1d8+6 and both claws 1d6+4 against a printed 1d6+4 bite and 1d4+4 claws.
defectsFound.cause: The Dire Ape used the shared native 1d6 bite and 1d4 claw, which do not override their damage dice, so the engine scales them one step up for a Large wielder. The Ape's slam is a project-owned weapon with its dice overridden and measured 1d6 correctly.
defectsFound.fix: The Dire Ape owns KMG.Summoning.Natural.DireApe.Bite1d6 and .Claw1d4, built by the same ConfigureWeapon path as the slam, which sets the override flag. The shared native weapons other creatures use are copied, never edited.
defectsFound.ledgerEffect: Two appended identities: 2980 to 2982, and the Sprint 18 append becomes 60 rather than 58.

defectsFound.observed: The Ape slammed for 1d6+3 with one limb and 1d6+2 with the other; the Dire Ape bit for one and a half times Strength while both claws carried one times it.
defectsFound.cause: RuleCalculateWeaponStats gives a natural weapon in the primary hand one and a half times the damage stat whenever the SECONDARY HAND is empty, and it never looks at the additional limbs. A creature whose other attacks are additional primary limbs therefore reads to the engine as a single-attack creature. Confirmed by reading the installed method rather than inferred.
defectsFound.fix: SummonPrimaryLimbFullStrength, attached to the two ape blueprints only, takes the difference back off the one limb the engine inflated, and only when the engine actually applied the multiplier to a Strength-driven primary-hand natural weapon on a body that really does carry additional limbs. No global rule is patched and a creature with a single natural attack keeps its one and a half times.

observerCorrections: The profile was read before the creature had acted, so it was flat-footed and denied its Dexterity in armour class, touch and combat manoeuvre defence. The review now reads the profile after the first full attack, which is the state a printed stat block describes.

In turn-based combat a command issued outside the owner's turn never resolves, so both turn-based routines measured zero attacks. The review now waits for the native turn controller to hand the unit its turn, ending other units' finished turns the way the qualified Sprint 16 cells do.

Resource release was counted in the same frame the unit was dismissed in, and native views are destroyed at the end of a frame. The review now lets the native teardown run before counting what survived.

The review required the donor's equipment renderer to stay enabled. The attachment never touches that flag, so its value is recorded rather than required; what is still required is that the renderer is present and blank.
runtimeRuns.restoration: VERIFIED; the live tree was restored to its pre-run hash

runtimeRuns.progression: 19/29, then 24/29, then 25/29, then 29/29. Each failure was diagnosed and fixed rather than accommodated.
findings: Run two proved the Dire Ape weapon fix: bite 1d6, claws 1d4 at Large.

Run two showed the full-Strength correction never fired, because a rulebook component is only subscribed when a unit fact carries it and it had been put on the blueprint's own component array. Moving it to a feature fixed it.
Run two showed every turn-based second sequence making no attacks: a native full attack costs the whole turn.

Run three named the last two points. The armour class modifier list reads Dexterity +2, Size -1, Natural Armour +3 and Difficulty -2 from the native DifficultOpponent feature, and Kingmaker derives combat manoeuvre defence from touch armour class, so that single term reached all four defensive numbers exactly once. It is the player's difficulty setting applied to every non-party creature, so the review subtracts it once and names it.

Run three lost a rend to a natural one, which always misses whatever the bonus. The review now re-attempts such a sequence up to four times and records every attempt with its d20, bonus and target armour class.

Both bodies authored as original project-owned geometry on the census-chosen rig, reviewed offline in clay, silhouette, textured and unlit across rest, slam, contact, rake, crouch, jaw-open and curled-hand poses, and wired through a creature-scoped view patch that swaps only this one instance and restores it exactly.

acceptedDeviations: The knuckle-walking gait is not authored. The engine plays the donor rig's own clips, which belong to a large upright biped; the geometry is an ape and the locomotion is the donor's.
The rend animation variant is not played: the engine selects it from its command-level rend gate, which this sprint does not use. The rend is still a visible damage event.
